editorial:
Imagine you are hanging out with friends and sharing scary stories about your old school. That is exactly the vibe you get here. You get three different spooky tales set in classrooms and nurse offices. Since this was made for TV, it feels very raw and grounded. You will meet students and teachers who stumble upon cursed videos and ghosts that just will not leave them alone. The atmosphere is heavy and creepy, making you feel like something is always watching from the corner of the room.

What really works is how the movie builds tension without relying on loud noises. The acting feels real, and the slow build-up to the scares is great. Some parts might feel a bit slow if you want non-stop action, but the twists make it worth it. If you love J-horror, you should definitely track this down.
endingExplained: The final segments wrap up with a chilling realization that the ghosts are not just random spirits. In the last story, the cycle of horror continues as the curse spreads to new people. You see that once you interact with the ghosts or the cursed objects, there is no real way to escape. It ends on a dark note, leaving you with the feeling that the hauntings will keep happening to anyone who enters those school halls.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic Japanese ghost stories and slow-build tension.
